messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: tenant_request_tail_latency.novahealth 99p > 5s (sustained 3m). Triggering SLA-breach pager (pd-ops). Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1815001234
Alex K: I'm oncall, grabbing it. Any customer-visible errors besides latency?
Priya M: Seeing increased 95/99p on model-inference-prod for that tenant. Errors are very low, so it's tail latency + long-running completions. Likely heavy long-prompt burst.
Jamie R: Can we mute noisy pagers for the tenant while we triage? We should avoid paging for every spike if it's a known batchy workload.
Alex K: Muting pager for tenant-specific SLA alerts for 20m (will keep critical infra alerts). Command: `oncall-bot mute-alert --alert tenant_request_tail_latency.novahealth --duration 20m --reason "triage & mitigate"`
oncall-bot: Executed: tenant_request_tail_latency.novahealth muted for 20m by Alex K. Pager overrides: false.
Priya M: Quick datapoints from dashboards: requests/s for novahealth jumped from 12 -> 78 over a 2m window. 98% of those requests are long prompts (>2048 tokens). KV cache miss ratio spiked due to new prompt variety.
Priya M: Logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:40Z worker-7 INFO request_id=xyZ tenant=novahealth model=gptx-16k latency=4760ms tokens=3100 kv_cache_status=miss
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z worker-4 INFO request_id=abC tenant=novahealth model=gptx-16k latency=5120ms tokens=4200 kv_cache_status=miss
```
Jamie R: Immediate mitigations I propose: 1) apply per-tenant throttle at the edge for novahealth (soft limit 40 rps) 2) temporarily route novahealth to model variant gptx-8k-ll for quicker responses, 3) create a tenant-scoped alert with rate-limited paging (eg: page only if sustained 5m and impact > 10% of requests). Thoughts?
Alex K: +1 on edge throttle and model fallback. I'll run the throttle now. Command: `curl -X POST https://edge-admin.internal/tenants/novahealth/actions -d '{"action":"throttle","rps":40}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx'`
Alex K: Throttle applied at 09:18 UTC. Observability note: added a temp tag `mitigation:novahealth-2026-03-15` to incoming traces.
Sam L: I'm drafting a customer note to NovaHealth support: "We're investigating elevated tail latency affecting some long prompt workloads. We've put temporary throttles and a lower-latency model in place; minimal risk to correctness. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Want me to send to acct manager?
Priya M: After throttle + fallback: 99p dropped from 5.2s -> 630ms within ~2m. 95p ~ 420ms. Looks like fallback helps and less concurrency reduced KV contention.
Alex K: Nice. Can someone make the temporary mitigation visible on the incidents dashboard and add a short timeline? That will help handoffs.
Taylor S: I'll take second shift handoff at 09:40 UTC. Summary I'll use: "NovaHealth SLA noise — root cause: sudden high-volume long prompts -> KV cache cold misses -> model fallback to slower execution path. Mitigations: edge throttle 40rps, model fallback to gptx-8k-ll, muted tenant SLA pager for 20m."
Taylor S: Handoff tasks I'll own: 1) keep throttles for next 1h and watch for customer complaints 2) request infra to prewarm KV cache tails (Priya) 3) create tenant-scoped dashboard panels (Alex) 4) propose alert tuning PR (Jamie)
Jamie R: For alert tuning, propose changing rule to: page only if `rate(requests{tenant="novahealth"}[5m]) > 30` AND `quantile(0.99, latency_ms{tenant="novahealth"}[5m]) > 3000`. Also add `for: 5m` and `labels: {severity: "page", tenant: "novahealth"}`. For noisy checks, add `runbook_link` and `mitigation_playbook` metadata. Example rule snippet:
```
- alert: NovaHealth_Tenant_Tail_Latency
  expr: rate(requests{tenant="novahealth"}[5m]) > 30 and quantile_over_time(0.99, latency_ms{tenant="novahealth"}[5m]) > 3000
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
    tenant: novahealth
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/novahealth-tail-latency
```
Alex K: +1. Also recommend adding an auto-silence window if the same tenant caused >3 pages in last 24h, to prevent noisy repeated pagings while allowing real infra issues to still escalate.
Priya M: I'll file infra ticket to add a background prewarm job for KV caches for high-traffic tenants and estimate effort. Assigning to infra-team with label `prewarm-kv-cache` and linking this thread.
Sam L: Sent a note to the NovaHealth AM and support: "We've implemented temporary mitigations and will follow up with a detailed timeline and actions. No data loss. Working on long-term fixes and alert tuning." They acknowledged (:thumbsup:).
oncall-bot: Reminder: muted alert will auto-unmute at 09:38 UTC.
Priya M: By 09:28 UTC both latency and error patterns are stable. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.
Taylor S: Post-incident items (I'll own):
- Create tenant-specific dashboard tiles (latency percentiles, rps, kv_cache_miss) by EOD tomorrow.
- PR to alerting repo with tuned rule + rate-limited paging (Jamie assigned).
- Runbook update with explicit mitigation steps: edge throttle, model fallback, contact flow for AM (Sam).
- Add NovaHealth to watchlist for 72h.
Alex K: Thanks team. Closing active paging. Leave thread for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
Priya M: Quick note for postmortem: include request size distribution, token growth, and whether recent client changes correlate.
Jamie R: I'll open the alerting PR now and link it here (PR: https://git.redwood/alerts/pull/452).
Taylor S: Taking handoff. If anything spikes, ping me @Taylor S or escalate to pd-ops.
Alex K: End of oncall update. Good job everyone. :speaker_high_volume:
